scenes.heading: Redox reactions
scenes.say: Batteries, breathing, bleach and rust all have one thing in common. Electrons move from one substance to another. These are redox reactions.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: You send $20 to a mate: you lose it, they gain it
scenes.science: One substance loses electrons, another gains them
scenes.breaks: in many molecules electrons are only shared unequally, not fully handed over, so we use oxidation numbers.
scenes.say: When you pay a mate twenty dollars on a banking app, you lose twenty and they gain twenty. The money can't vanish. In redox, electrons are the money. The substance that loses electrons is oxidised, and the one that gains them is reduced. The two always happen together.
scenes.caption: When you pay a mate $20 on a banking app, you lose $20 and they gain $20. The money can't vanish. In redox, electrons are the money. The substance that loses electrons is oxidised, and the one that gains them is reduced. The two always happen together.

scenes.heading: OIL RIG
scenes.say: Remember OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain, of electrons. Careful with agents: they do the opposite of their name. The oxidising agent gets reduced, and the reducing agent gets oxidised.

scenes.heading: Oxidation numbers
points: O is usually −2; H is usually +1
Numbers add up to the overall charge
Goes up: oxidised. Goes down: reduced
scenes.say: Oxidation numbers help track electrons. Elements are zero. Oxygen is usually minus two and hydrogen plus one. They add up to the overall charge. If an atom's number goes up, it's oxidised. If it goes down, it's reduced.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Find the oxidation number of Mn in MnO₄⁻.
scenes.say: What's the oxidation number of manganese in permanganate? Call it x. Four oxygens at minus two give minus eight. The total must equal the ion's charge, minus one. So x minus eight equals minus one, and x is plus seven.

scenes.heading: KOHES: half-equations in acid
steps: Electrons: to the more positive side
scenes.say: To balance half-equations in acid, use KOHES. Balance the key element. Balance oxygen with water. Balance hydrogen with H plus. Add electrons to the more positive side. Then add states. To combine half-equations, make the electrons match like a handshake, then cancel them.
scenes.caption: To balance half-equations in acid, use KOHES. Balance the key element. Balance oxygen with water. Balance hydrogen with H⁺. Add electrons to the more positive side. Then add states. To combine half-equations, make the electrons match like a handshake, then cancel them.

scenes.heading: Displacement and rust
points: More reactive metal displaces less reactive ions
Iron rusts with water AND oxygen
Barriers like paint keep them out
scenes.say: A more reactive metal displaces the ions of a less reactive one. Iron rusts when it's oxidised with water and oxygen. Paint keeps them out. Or attach a more reactive metal, like zinc or magnesium. It acts like a bodyguard, getting oxidised instead of the iron.

points: OIL RIG: loss = oxidation, gain = reduction
Agents do the opposite of their name
scenes.say: Quick recap. Oxidation is loss and reduction is gain of electrons. Agents do the opposite of their name. An oxidation number going up means oxidised. And KOHES balances half-equations. Now try the practice questions!
